8d731d1349f87fb20a693ece8c1ba0a10d95004b.title: Compact Causal Range
8d731d1349f87fb20a693ece8c1ba0a10d95004b.body:
Fix \(n\), and let \(P\) be a transported array with sample-size and envelope schedules \(N_n\) and \(k_n\), constants \(c\) and \(\varepsilon\), and model class \(\mathcal P_n\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) at the index \(n\).
\item \textbf{(Source contrasts.)} The assignment outcome contrast and the receipt contrast for the source population satisfy the usual measurability and integrability conditions under the source covariate marginal \(P_S^X\).
\end{itemize}
Then \(\Delta_Y\) and \(\Delta_D\) represent the observed source outcome and receipt contrasts: for every measurable covariate set \(A\),
\[
\int_{\{O:X\in A\}} H(O)Y\,dP_S(O)
=
\int_A \Delta_Y(x)\,dP_S^X(x),
\qquad
\int_{\{O:X\in A\}} H(O)D\,dP_S(O)
=
\int_A \Delta_D(x)\,dP_S^X(x).
\]
Moreover, the transported reduced-form outcome mean satisfies
\[
\mu_{Y,n}
=
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[
\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}\mathbf 1\{D(1)=1,\ D(0)=0\}\mid S=0
\right],
\]
the transported first-stage mean satisfies
\[
\mu_n
=
P_n^F\{D(1)=1,\ D(0)=0\mid S=0\},
\]
and the Wald ratio equals the target complier-conditional contrast,
\[
\frac{\mu_{Y,n}}{\mu_n}=\theta_T.
\]
Finally, \(\theta_T\in\Theta=[-1,1]\).

9bdf65ee2586f14ef001d067d3d2d8130b7aef13.title: Oracle Score Attainment
9bdf65ee2586f14ef001d067d3d2d8130b7aef13.body:
Fix sequences \(N_n\) and \(k_n\), constants \(c,\varepsilon,\alpha\), and the transported-IV model class \(\mathcal P_n\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling ratio.)} \(c>0\) and \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap and noncoverage.)} \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope scale.)} \(k_n>0\) for every \(n\), \(k_n\to\infty\), and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Admissible geometry.)} There is an admissible deterministic geometry \(\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}\) at scale \(k_n\) and overlap constant \(\varepsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform model restrictions.)} Every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) satisfies the two-sample condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}\), the overlap condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap}\), the weight envelope in \(\cref{obj:ass:weight-envelope}\), the weight second-moment bound in \(\cref{obj:ass:weight-second-moment}\), and the degrading-array condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:degrading-array}\).
\end{itemize}
Let
\[
L_\alpha=\left(\frac{8}{\alpha\varepsilon^2}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
For each \(n\), define
\[
H_i=\frac{Z_i}{e(X_i)}-\frac{1-Z_i}{1-e(X_i)},\qquad
\widehat A_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n w(X_i)H_iY_i,\qquad
\widehat B_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n w(X_i)H_iD_i,
\]
and
\[
\widehat\kappa_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n w(X_i)^2,\qquad
C_n=\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
\left|\widehat A_n-\vartheta\widehat B_n\right|
\le L_\alpha\sqrt{\frac{\widehat\kappa_n}{n}}\right\}.
\]
Then the score-inversion sequence \((C_n)\) belongs to the oracle honest class \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:oracle-honesty}\).  Moreover, with
\[
C_0=\max\left\{2,\ 4L_\alpha+\frac8{\varepsilon^2}\right\},
\]
for every \(t_0>0\),
\[
R((C_n),t_0)\le C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
Consequently the oracle value in \(\cref{obj:def:oracle-value}\) satisfies the same attainable frontier order over fixed positive effective-strength thresholds.

54f7fa6fe8f2f17298586760622d4c82a2393b86.title: Single-Population Frontier Reduction
54f7fa6fe8f2f17298586760622d4c82a2393b86.body:
On a measurable covariate space \(\mathcal X\), let \(\mathfrak g\) be a deterministic geometry array satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}\) with scale \(k_n\) and overlap constant \(\varepsilon\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling ratio.)} \(c>0\) and \(N_n/n \to c\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap and noncoverage.)} \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Cell scale.)} \(k_n>0\) for every \(n\), \(k_n\to\infty\), and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to 0\).
\item \textbf{(Unit transport weight.)} For every \(n\), \(w_n(X)=1\) \(P_{S,n}^X\)-almost surely under \(\mathfrak g\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(n\),
\[
\kappa_n=1
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
P_{T,n}=P_{S,n}^X .
\]
Moreover, for every transported array \(P\) and every \(n\), if \(P\in\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-slice}\), then its effective strength satisfies
\[
t_n
=
n\mu_n^2 .
\]
Finally, for every \(t_0>0\), let
\[
L_\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{8}{\alpha\varepsilon^2}},
\qquad
c_\alpha=\frac{3(1-\alpha)^2}{16},
\qquad
C_\alpha=\max\left\{2,\;4L_\alpha+\frac{8}{\varepsilon^2}\right\}.
\]
The fixed-geometry minimax value \(V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-value}\) obeys
\[
c_\alpha \min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
\le
V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)
\le
C_\alpha \min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]

638f6fbeb2a2e554399a58ee7ac1f63fba9a4d0c.title: Oracle Frontier Converse
638f6fbeb2a2e554399a58ee7ac1f63fba9a4d0c.body:
Fix \(c>0\), \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  There exist constants \(c_0>0\) and \(t_c>0\), depending on \(c\), \(\varepsilon\), and \(\alpha\), such that the following holds.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Array size.)} The target sample sizes satisfy \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Cell scale.)} The sequence \(k_n\) is positive, satisfies \(k_n\to\infty\), and satisfies \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Measurable finite carriers.)} For each \(n\), the covariate space contains \(k_n\) distinct measurable singleton carrier cells.
\item \textbf{(Transported-IV class.)} Every array in the transported model class \(\mathcal P_n\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class} satisfies \cref{obj:ass:full-data-support,obj:ass:population-presence,obj:ass:two-sample-array,obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:source-observation,obj:ass:iv-randomization,obj:ass:iv-exclusion,obj:ass:iv-monotonicity,obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport,obj:ass:target-complier-positivity,obj:ass:transport-domination,obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array}.
\item \textbf{(Finite-cell submodel.)} Every array in the finite-cell class \(\mathcal N_n\) of \cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class} satisfies \cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}.
\end{itemize}

Then, for every \(t_0>0\), the oracle values of \cref{obj:def:oracle-value,obj:def:finite-cell-oracle-value} obey
\[
c_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\le V^\star(t_0)
\]
and
\[
c_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}\le V_{\mathcal N}^\star(t_0).
\]
Moreover, for every \(t_0\in(0,t_c]\),
\[
c_0\le V^\star(t_0).
\]
The same constants \(c_0\) and \(t_c\) apply uniformly over all decompositions of the effective strength \(t_0\) into the transported first-stage mean \(\mu_n\) and the weight dispersion \(\kappa_n\).

b5f2ad496eccaf685aff8bc32a97c20014dcefd0.title: Fixed Geometry Frontier
b5f2ad496eccaf685aff8bc32a97c20014dcefd0.body:
Let \(c>0\), let \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), and let \(0<\alpha<1\). Let \(N_n\) satisfy \(N_n/n\to c\), and let \(k_n\) be positive with \(k_n\to\infty\) and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\). Fix a deterministic geometry array \(\mathfrak g\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}\). Assume that, for every \(n\) and every law \(P_n^F\in\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-slice}\), the conditions in
\(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array,obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array}\)
hold.

For \(t_0>0\), define
\[
L_\alpha=\left(\frac{8}{\alpha\varepsilon^2}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
c_\alpha=\frac{3(1-\alpha)^2}{16},
\qquad
C_\alpha=\max\left\{2,\,4L_\alpha+\frac{8}{\varepsilon^2}\right\}.
\]
Then the fixed-geometry minimax value of \(\cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-value}\) satisfies
\[
c_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
\le
V_{\mathfrak g}^{\star}(t_0)
\le
C_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
The displayed constants are uniform over admissible deterministic geometries \(\mathfrak g\).

b6bc60215d29ce1a74988f555bca0b3688150181.title: Regular Cell Weight Attainment
b6bc60215d29ce1a74988f555bca0b3688150181.body:
Fix \(c,\varepsilon,\alpha,c_-,c_+\in\mathbb R\) and sequences \(N_n\) and \(k_n\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample-size ratio.)} \(0<c\) and \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap and coverage levels.)} \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Regular cell constants.)} \(0<c_-\le 1\) and \(1\le c_+\).
\item \textbf{(Cell growth.)} \(k_n>0\) for every \(n\), \(k_n\to\infty\), and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Measurable carrier.)} For every \(n\), the covariate carrier contains \(k_n\) injected measurable singleton cells.
\item \textbf{(Model restrictions.)} Every array \(P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:regular-finite-cell-class}\) with constants \(c,\varepsilon,c_-,c_+\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}\), \(\cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap}\), and \(\cref{obj:ass:degrading-array}\).
\end{itemize}
On \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), let \(q_{x,n}=P_S^X(X=x)\) and define
\[
H_i=\frac{Z_i}{e(X_i)}-\frac{1-Z_i}{1-e(X_i)}.
\]
For \(G\in\{Y,D\}\), set
\[
\widehat p_{x,n}=\frac1{N_n}\sum_{j=1}^{N_n}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=x\},
\qquad
\widehat m_{G,n}(x)=\frac1{nq_{x,n}}\sum_{i=1}^n
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}H_iG_i,
\]
and
\[
\widehat M_{G,n}=\sum_{x=1}^{k_n}\widehat p_{x,n}\widehat m_{G,n}(x).
\]
For \(N_n\ge2\), set
\[
\widehat\kappa_{U,n}
=
\frac1{N_n(N_n-1)}\sum_{j\ne\ell}
\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=X_\ell^T\}}{q_{X_j^T,n}},
\qquad
\widehat K_n=1+\widehat\kappa_{U,n},
\]
and put \(C_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\Theta\) when \(N_n<2\).  Let
\[
B_{\varepsilon,c}=8(\varepsilon^{-2}+c^{-1}).
\]
For every fixed \(L\ge\{2B_{\varepsilon,c}/\alpha\}^{1/2}\), the sequence
\[
C_n^{\mathrm{reg}}
=
\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
|\widehat M_{Y,n}-\vartheta\widehat M_{D,n}|
\le L\sqrt{\widehat K_n/n}\right\}
\]
for \(N_n\ge2\), together with the preceding convention for \(N_n<2\), belongs to \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:regular-cell-feasible-honesty}\) and is constructed from the known regular source-cell probabilities, the known propensity, and the source and target samples.  Moreover, for every fixed \(t_0>0\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}:\,t_n\ge t_0}
\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n^{\mathrm{reg}})]
\le
\max\{2,4\sqrt2L+8B_{\varepsilon,c}\}
\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
The corresponding minimax risk over \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}\) is bounded below by
\[
\frac{3(1-\alpha)^2}{16}\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
Thus, with known regular source-cell probabilities and a known cell-varying propensity satisfying the stated overlap, the feasible regular-cell construction attains the oracle frontier order on \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).

ad22386500f7b8544bbf8536f2d545a0066283fc.title: Finite-Cell Weight Attainment
ad22386500f7b8544bbf8536f2d545a0066283fc.body:
Let \(N_n\) and \(k_n\) be positive integer sequences, let \(c,\varepsilon,\alpha\in\mathbb R\), and suppose the following conditions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling ratio.)} \(c>0\) and \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap and coverage levels.)} \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Cell growth.)} \(k_n>0\) for every \(n\), \(k_n\to\infty\), and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Ambient carrier.)} For every \(n\), the measurable covariate space contains \(k_n\) distinct measurable singleton cells.
\item \textbf{(Finite-cell rows.)} For every row \(n\) and every transported array \(P\in\mathcal N_n\), the row satisfies the two-sample condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}\), the uniform finite-cell source condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}\), and the degrading-array condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:degrading-array}\), with \(\mathcal N_n\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class}\).
\end{itemize}
Put
\[
B_c=32(1+c^{-1}),\qquad
L_{\alpha,c}=\left(\frac{2B_c}{\alpha}\right)^{1/2},\qquad
C_0=\max\{2,4\sqrt2\,L_{\alpha,c}+8B_c\}.
\]
Then \(C_0>0\), and there exists a sample-only finite-cell confidence-set sequence \(C=(C_n)\) in the feasible class \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{cell}}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:finite-cell-feasible-honesty}\) such that, for every \(n\) and every \(P\in\mathcal N_n\), \(C_n\) agrees \(P\)-almost surely with the finite-cell score-inversion rule using critical constant \(L_{\alpha,c}\). Equivalently, on the finite-cell experiment, this rule is given by
\[
H_i=2(2Z_i-1),\qquad
\widehat p_{x,n}=\frac1{N_n}\sum_{j=1}^{N_n}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=x\},
\]
and, for \(G\in\{Y,D\}\),
\[
\widehat m_{G,n}(x)=\frac{k_n}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}H_iG_i,\qquad
\widehat M_{G,n}=\sum_{x=1}^{k_n}\widehat p_{x,n}\widehat m_{G,n}(x).
\]
For \(N_n\ge2\), define
\[
\widehat\kappa_{U,n}
=\frac{k_n}{N_n(N_n-1)}
\sum_{j\ne\ell}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=X_\ell^T\},\qquad
\widehat K_n=1+\widehat\kappa_{U,n},
\]
and set
\[
C_n=\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
|\widehat M_{Y,n}-\vartheta\widehat M_{D,n}|
\le L_{\alpha,c}\sqrt{\widehat K_n/n}\right\},
\]
with \(C_n=\Theta\) at indices for which \(N_n<2\). For every \(t_0>0\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n:\,t_n\ge t_0}
\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)]
\le
C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
Moreover, for every \(t_0>0\), the feasible finite-cell honest minimax risk satisfies
\[
\frac{3(1-\alpha)^2}{16}\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde C\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{cell}}}
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n:\,t_n\ge t_0}
\mathbb E_P[\lambda(\widetilde C_n)].
\]

9b5a2204eee279bab1d018f9bdc466298ea93705.title: Full-data support
9b5a2204eee279bab1d018f9bdc466298ea93705.body:
The full-data law satisfies
\[
P_n^F\{S\in\{0,1\},\ D(0),D(1)\in\{0,1\},\ Y(0),Y(1)\in[0,1]\}=1.
\]

2559f8cd0d69a59773a8ec39b2a57ad7548b0b69.title: Two-sample array
2559f8cd0d69a59773a8ec39b2a57ad7548b0b69.body:
The source and target samples satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Source sample.)} \((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n\sim P_S^{\otimes n}\).
\item \textbf{(Target sample.)} \((X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}\sim P_T^{\otimes N_n}\).
\item \textbf{(Independence.)} \((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n\perp (X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}\).
\item \textbf{(Sample-size ratio.)} \(N_n/n\to c\).
\end{itemize}

0f74befeecb5b371dd6d31ca4bc5727375602fe4.title: Instrument overlap
0f74befeecb5b371dd6d31ca4bc5727375602fe4.body:
The source propensity score satisfies
\[
\varepsilon\le e(X)\le 1-\varepsilon
\]
\(P_S\)-almost surely.

a23cbd16aa05d23f79118523cc1e26b5b295bd26.title: Source observation law

d21ed5c0fd4c97e278d99f7e25b236454aa27ac0.title: Instrument exclusion
d21ed5c0fd4c97e278d99f7e25b236454aa27ac0.body:
For every \(z,s\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Y^Z(z)=Y(D(z))
\]
\(P_n^F\)-almost surely conditional on \(S=s\).

1f0b770779946ef9447ca0cce1740f1beb74582b.title: Instrument monotonicity
1f0b770779946ef9447ca0cce1740f1beb74582b.body:
For every \(s\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
D(1)\ge D(0)
\]
\(P_n^F\)-almost surely conditional on \(S=s\).

f94795d2994ada4dd5a2cc76ba8ae308a5df9a45.title: Outcome-contrast transport
f94795d2994ada4dd5a2cc76ba8ae308a5df9a45.body:
For \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=0\right]
=
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=1\right].
\]

2164e55a41cb9d14f8f52800a3e18ba905d045ab.title: Receipt-contrast transport
2164e55a41cb9d14f8f52800a3e18ba905d045ab.body:
The target-population average of the conditional treatment-receipt contrast agrees across the two population states:
\[
\mathbb E_{X\mid S=0}\!\left[
  \mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[D(1)-D(0)\mid X,S=0\right]
\right]
=
\mathbb E_{X\mid S=0}\!\left[
  \mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[D(1)-D(0)\mid X,S=1\right]
\right].
\]

281212ab95c0f9898e1741bbac6d094db8553f41.title: Target complier positivity
281212ab95c0f9898e1741bbac6d094db8553f41.body:
The target population has positive complier mass:
\[
P_n^F\!\left(D(1)>D(0)\mid S=0\right)>0.
\]

52a3aa81a46f04a79628c52cd4bc327607fcaf59.title: Transport domination
52a3aa81a46f04a79628c52cd4bc327607fcaf59.body:
The target covariate law is absolutely continuous with respect to the source covariate marginal on \(\mathcal X\):
\[
P_T\ll P_S^X.
\]

da1ae2d50b01e260ce55b62c7e32a6327af71c92.title: Weight envelope
da1ae2d50b01e260ce55b62c7e32a6327af71c92.body:
The transport weight satisfies
\[
0 \le w(X) \le 2k_n
\]
\(P_S\)-almost surely.

fc78268fcffb57a33f359e9f8fb3f212c9b15942.title: Weight second moment
fc78268fcffb57a33f359e9f8fb3f212c9b15942.body:
The second moment of the transport weight satisfies
\[
\kappa_n \le k_n .
\]

bda5561c6cc5792604b08a8232a04c3b4320f918.title: Uniform finite cells
bda5561c6cc5792604b08a8232a04c3b4320f918.body:
The source covariate marginal \(P_S^X\) is supported on exactly \(k_n\) measurable cells, assigns mass \(1/k_n\) to each cell, and satisfies
\[
e(X)=1/2
\]
\(P_S\)-almost surely.

a7e60189d76c4e6f8baeb580b4866674ea972b3d.title: Transported LATE model class \(\mathcal P_n\)
a7e60189d76c4e6f8baeb580b4866674ea972b3d.body:
The transported LATE model class at index \(n\) is
\[
\mathcal P_n
=
\bigl\{(P_n^F,e): (P_n^F,e)\text{ satisfies the following conditions at index }n\bigr\}.
\]
The required conditions are:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Full-data support.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:full-data-support}\).
\item \textbf{(Population presence.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:population-presence}\).
\item \textbf{(Two-sample array.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument overlap.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap}\).
\item \textbf{(Source observation.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:source-observation}\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument randomization.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:iv-randomization}\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument exclusion.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:iv-exclusion}\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument monotonicity.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:iv-monotonicity}\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome transport.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:outcome-transport}\).
\item \textbf{(Receipt transport.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:receipt-transport}\).
\item \textbf{(Target complier positivity.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:target-complier-positivity}\).
\item \textbf{(Transport domination.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:transport-domination}\).
\item \textbf{(Weight envelope.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:weight-envelope}\).
\item \textbf{(Weight second moment.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:weight-second-moment}\).
\item \textbf{(Degrading array.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:degrading-array}\).
\end{itemize}

bf2f87d04db43a6e0259c453433742f4fa84dfdb.title: Finite-cell class \(\mathcal N_n\)
bf2f87d04db43a6e0259c453433742f4fa84dfdb.body:
The finite-cell submodel at index \(n\) is
\[
\mathcal N_n
=
\bigl\{P\in\mathcal P_n: P\text{ satisfies the following conditions at index }n\bigr\}.
\]
The required conditions are:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Full-data support.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:full-data-support}\).
\item \textbf{(Population presence.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:population-presence}\).
\item \textbf{(Two-sample array.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument overlap.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap}\).
\item \textbf{(Source observation.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:source-observation}\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument randomization.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:iv-randomization}\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument exclusion.)} \(\cref{obj:ass:iv-exclusion}\).

6c2fa107d791d7b097024ef889482e36d8c75ce5.title: Oracle honest class $\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}$
6c2fa107d791d7b097024ef889482e36d8c75ce5.body:
The oracle honest class is
\[
\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}
=
\left\{
(C_n)_{n\ge 1}:
C_n
=
C_n\!\left((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n},w,e\right)
\subseteq \Theta,\ 
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P(\theta_T\in C_n)
\ge 1-\alpha
\right\}.
\]

dbd745fce670730a9e38bafdc1b369fbe3b93576.title: Frontier risk $R((C_n),t_0)$
dbd745fce670730a9e38bafdc1b369fbe3b93576.body:
For a confidence-set sequence \((C_n)_{n\ge1}\) and threshold \(t_0\), the limiting worst-case expected length above effective strength \(t_0\) is
\[
R((C_n),t_0)
=
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n:\,t_n\ge t_0}
\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)].
\]

2120c08f1cf7ce312dd692933f1f7fc16b6f8692.title: Oracle value $V^\star(t_0)$
2120c08f1cf7ce312dd692933f1f7fc16b6f8692.body:
The oracle minimax expected-length value at threshold \(t_0\) is
\[
V^\star(t_0)
=
\inf_{(C_n)\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}}
R((C_n),t_0).
\]

218f007f5930e0a74a92a22aa530db4a0c099bb5.title: Feasible finite-cell class $\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{cell}}$
218f007f5930e0a74a92a22aa530db4a0c099bb5.body:
The feasible finite-cell honest class is
\[
\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{cell}}
=
\left\{
(C_n)_{n\ge1}:
C_n
=
C_n\!\left((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}\right)
\subseteq\Theta,\ 
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal N_n}
P(\theta_T\in C_n)
\ge 1-\alpha
\right\}.
\]

47eebe285e86747d26a08b0e7a15ebf5b1cbbacc.title: Score-inversion set $C_n$
47eebe285e86747d26a08b0e7a15ebf5b1cbbacc.body:
For each \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), define the source score
\[
w(X)\left\{\frac{Z}{e(X)}-\frac{1-Z}{1-e(X)}\right\}(Y-\vartheta D).
\]
With oracle-known \(w\) and \(e\), the score-inversion confidence set is
\[
C_n
=
\left\{
\vartheta\in\Theta:
\left|
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
w(X_i)\left\{\frac{Z_i}{e(X_i)}-\frac{1-Z_i}{1-e(X_i)}\right\}(Y_i-\vartheta D_i)
\right|
\le
L_\alpha
\left\{
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{w(X_i)^2}{n}
\right\}^{1/2}
\right\}.
\]
For oracle-known \(w\) and \(e\), this score is a source-sample statistic.

ce360cd20970dfecb7704941b0742b568ee85c08.title: Geometry handle \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\)
ce360cd20970dfecb7704941b0742b568ee85c08.body:
Fix an admissible deterministic array \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\). For \(t_0>0\), set
\[
\mu_n=\left(\frac{t_0\kappa_n}{n}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
p_n(x)=\frac{\mu_n w(x)}{\kappa_n}.
\]
For \(0<\alpha<1\), let \(\rho=(1-\alpha)/8\). As the complier outcome mean varies over \(h\in\mathbb R\) with
\[
|h|\le \min\{1/4,\rho t_0^{-1/2}\},
\]
the corresponding least-favorable laws satisfy
\[
1+\chi^2(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\Vert Q_{n,0}^{\mathfrak g})
\le \exp(8t_0h^2),
\qquad
\|Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}-Q_{n,0}^{\mathfrak g}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le 2\rho .
\]

f6c0747876b0079e74732716034b8540b0d2466f.title: Least-favorable witness \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\)
f6c0747876b0079e74732716034b8540b0d2466f.body:
Fix \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\in\mathcal G\) and \(t_0>0\). Set
\[
\mu_n=\left(\frac{t_0\kappa_n}{n}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
p_n(x)=\frac{\mu_n w(x)}{\kappa_n},
\qquad
\rho=\frac{1-\alpha}{8},
\qquad
H(t_0)=\min\{1/4,\rho t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
For each \(|h|\le H(t_0)\), conditional on \(X=x\), assign compliance types by
\[
\Pr\{(D(0),D(1))=(0,1)\mid X=x\}=p_n(x),
\]
\[
\Pr\{(D(0),D(1))=(1,1)\mid X=x\}
=
\Pr\{(D(0),D(1))=(0,0)\mid X=x\}
=
\frac{1-p_n(x)}{2}.
\]
Set \(Y(0)=0\). For compliers, let \(Y(1)\) be Bernoulli with mean \(1/2+h\); for always-takers and never-takers, let \(Y(1)\) be Bernoulli with mean \(1/2\). Use this same conditional full-data law in both populations, draw source encouragement with propensity \(e(X)\), and write \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\) for the resulting joint observed-data law together with the fixed oracle inputs.

856d4137618a7b0ff6e9d2acb9979a0d0006851c.title: Admissible geometry class \(\mathcal G\)
856d4137618a7b0ff6e9d2acb9979a0d0006851c.body:
\(\mathcal G\) is the class of deterministic arrays \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\) satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Source law.)} \(P_S^X\) is a probability law on \(\mathcal X\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument overlap.)} \(e:\mathcal X\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
\item \textbf{(Transport weights.)} \(w:\mathcal X\to[0,2k_n]\), \(\mathbb E_S[w(X)]=1\), and
\[
\kappa_n=\mathbb E_S[w(X)^2]\le k_n .
\]
\item \textbf{(Target law.)} For every measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\),
\[
P_T(A)=\mathbb E_S\!\left[w(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in A\}\right].
\]
\end{itemize}

0172c301fb43fae515c322f91bb3846692aa030d.title: Fixed-geometry slice \(\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\)
0172c301fb43fae515c322f91bb3846692aa030d.body:
For \(\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G\),
\[
\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P_n:
(P_S^X,w,e)\text{ equals the index-}n\text{ component of }\mathfrak g
\right\}.
\]

821c23ed62a854f22a55390cca6963720b677e94.title: Fixed-geometry oracle honesty \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathfrak g)\)
821c23ed62a854f22a55390cca6963720b677e94.body:
For \(\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}\), \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathfrak g)\) is the class of sequences \((C_n)_{n\ge1}\) such that
\[
C_n
=
C_n\!\left((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n},w,e\right)
\subseteq \Theta
\]
and
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)}
P(\theta_T\in C_n)
\ge 1-\alpha .
\]

24016af7f9df4778038ad4458a1f9ae30c80d13d.title: Fixed-Geometry Frontier
24016af7f9df4778038ad4458a1f9ae30c80d13d.body:
Let \(c>0\), \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), and \(0<\alpha<1\). Assume the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Target-sample ratio.)} The target sample sizes satisfy \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope scale.)} The sequence \(k_n\) is positive for every \(n\), satisfies \(k_n\to\infty\), and obeys \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Geometry.)} The deterministic geometry array \(\mathfrak g\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}\) with scale \(k_n\) and overlap constant \(\varepsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Fixed-geometry slices.)} For every \(n\) and every transported array whose \(n\)th law lies in the fixed-geometry slice \(\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-slice}\), the conditions in
\(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array,obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array}\)
hold.
\end{itemize}

For every \(t_0>0\), define
\[
L_\alpha=\left(\frac{8}{\alpha\varepsilon^2}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
c_\alpha=\frac{3(1-\alpha)^2}{16},
\qquad
C_\alpha=\max\left\{2,\,4L_\alpha+\frac{8}{\varepsilon^2}\right\}.
\]
Then the fixed-geometry minimax value of \(\cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-value}\) satisfies
\[
c_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
\le
V_{\mathfrak g}^{\star}(t_0)
\le
C_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
The constants \(c_\alpha\) and \(C_\alpha\) are uniform over admissible deterministic geometries \(\mathfrak g\).

6a9b3d557ee0f89f59e690a1f58a30390d98293f.title: Compact causal range
6a9b3d557ee0f89f59e690a1f58a30390d98293f.body:
Fix \(n\), \(P\), \(N_n\), \(k_n\), \(c\), and the instrument-overlap constant \(\varepsilon\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} \(P\) belongs to the transported complier-effect model class \(\mathcal P_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).
\item \textbf{(Source contrasts.)} The source conditional outcome contrast \(\Delta_Y(x)\) and the source conditional receipt contrast \(\Delta_D(x)\) are measurable and integrable with respect to the source covariate marginal \(P_S^X\).
\end{itemize}
Then \(\Delta_Y\) and \(\Delta_D\) represent the observed source contrasts: for every measurable covariate set \(A\),
\[
\int_{\{O^S:X\in A\}} H(O^S)Y\,dP_S
=
\int_A \Delta_Y(x)\,dP_S^X(x),
\qquad
\int_{\{O^S:X\in A\}} H(O^S)D\,dP_S
=
\int_A \Delta_D(x)\,dP_S^X(x).
\]
Moreover, with
\[
\mu_{Y,n}
=
\int \bigl(Y(1)-Y(0)\bigr)\mathbf 1\{D(1)=1,\ D(0)=0\}\,dP_n^F(\,\cdot\mid S=0)
\]
and
\[
\mu_n
=
P_n^F\{D(1)=1,\ D(0)=0\mid S=0\},
\]
the transported reduced-form and first-stage means satisfy
\[
\int w(x)\Delta_Y(x)\,dP_S^X(x)=\mu_{Y,n},
\qquad
\int w(x)\Delta_D(x)\,dP_S^X(x)=\mu_n.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\mu_{Y,n}}{\mu_n}
=
\theta_T
=
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid D(1)=1,\ D(0)=0,\ S=0\right]
\in \Theta=[-1,1].
\]

d144f8019baab0527db38f4ef8215e30871f1969.title: No-shift reduction
d144f8019baab0527db38f4ef8215e30871f1969.body:
Fix a measurable covariate space and deterministic arrays \(N_n\), \(k_n\), and \(\mathfrak g\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample-size ratio.)} \(c>0\) and \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Coverage and overlap constants.)} \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Cell-scale regime.)} For every \(n\), \(k_n>0\), with \(k_n\to\infty\) and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Admissible geometry.)} The geometry \(\mathfrak g\) belongs to the admissible class \(\mathcal G\) in \(\cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}\).
\item \textbf{(No covariate shift.)} For every \(n\), \(w_n(X)=1\) \(P_{S,n}^X\)-almost surely.
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(n\), the geometry has
\[
\kappa_n=\int w_n(x)^2\,dP_{S,n}^X(x)=1
\]
and \(P_{T,n}=P_{S,n}^X\). Moreover, for every transported array \(P_n^F\) in the fixed-geometry slice \(\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-slice}\),
\[
t_n=\frac{n\mu_n^2}{\kappa_n}=n\mu_n^2 .
\]
Finally, for every \(t_0>0\), define
\[
L_\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{8}{\alpha\varepsilon^2}},
\qquad
c_\alpha=\frac{3(1-\alpha)^2}{16},
\qquad
C_\alpha=\max\left\{2,\,4L_\alpha+\frac{8}{\varepsilon^2}\right\}.
\]
The fixed-geometry minimax value \(V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)\) in \(\cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-value}\) satisfies
\[
c_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
\le
V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)
\le
C_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]

af06d0eb5dbfb6188735657e6d99908b4e4c2368.title: Oracle converse frontier
af06d0eb5dbfb6188735657e6d99908b4e4c2368.body:
Fix \(c>0\), an instrument-overlap constant \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and a noncoverage level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). There exist constants \(c_0>0\) and \(t_c>0\), depending only on \((\alpha,\varepsilon,c)\), such that the following holds for every measurable covariate space \(\mathcal X\).

Let \(N_n\) and \(k_n\) be integer sequences satisfying
\[
  \frac{N_n}{n}\to c,
  \qquad
  k_n>0,\qquad
  k_n\to\infty,\qquad
  \frac{k_n}{\sqrt n}\to 0 .
\]
Assume that, for each \(n\), \(\mathcal X\) contains a measurable \(k_n\)-cell carrier, and that every array in \(\mathcal P_n\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:full-data-support,obj:ass:population-presence,obj:ass:two-sample-array,obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:source-observation,obj:ass:iv-randomization,obj:ass:iv-exclusion,obj:ass:iv-monotonicity,obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport,obj:ass:target-complier-positivity,obj:ass:transport-domination,obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array}\). Assume also that every array in the finite-cell class \(\mathcal N_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class}\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}\).

Then, for every effective-strength threshold \(t_0>0\),
\[
  c_0 \min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
  \le V^\star(t_0)
\]
and
\[
  c_0 \min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
  \le V_{\mathcal N}^\star(t_0),
\]
where \(V^\star(t_0)\) and \(V_{\mathcal N}^\star(t_0)\) are the oracle values in \(\cref{obj:def:oracle-value,obj:def:finite-cell-oracle-value}\). Moreover, whenever \(0<t_0\le t_c\),
\[
  c_0 \le V^\star(t_0).
\]

cb7a4801ff3ebfe68144c8b613e51a2b0d0544e1.title: Oracle score inversion
cb7a4801ff3ebfe68144c8b613e51a2b0d0544e1.body:
Let \(N_n\) and \(k_n\) be integer sequences, and let \(c\), \(\varepsilon\), and \(\alpha\) be constants.  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling ratio.)} \(c>0\) and \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap and coverage constants.)} \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope scale.)} \(k_n>0\) for every \(n\), \(k_n\to\infty\), and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Admissible geometry.)} The measurable covariate space admits a deterministic geometry \(\mathfrak g\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}\) with envelope scale \(k_n\) and overlap constant \(\varepsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Model-class implications.)} For every \(n\) and every transported array \(P\), membership of \(P\) in the transported complier-effect model class \(\mathcal P_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) implies \(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array,obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array}\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
L_\alpha=\left(\frac{8}{\alpha\varepsilon^2}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
H_i=\frac{Z_i}{e(X_i)}-\frac{1-Z_i}{1-e(X_i)},
\]
and
\[
\widehat A_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n w(X_i)H_iY_i,
\qquad
\widehat B_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n w(X_i)H_iD_i,
\qquad
\widehat\kappa_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n w(X_i)^2 .
\]
Let the score-inversion confidence set be
\[
C_n
=
\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
\left|\widehat A_n-\vartheta\widehat B_n\right|
\le
L_\alpha\sqrt{\widehat\kappa_n/n}
\right\}.
\]
Then the sequence \((C_n)\) is oracle honest, \((C_n)\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:oracle-honesty}\), and for every fixed effective-strength threshold \(t_0>0\),
\[
R((C_n),t_0)
\le
C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\},
\qquad
C_0=\max\left\{2,4L_\alpha+\frac8{\varepsilon^2}\right\}.
\]
Consequently, for the oracle minimax value \(V^\star(t_0)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:oracle-value}\),
\[
V^\star(t_0)
\le
C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]

c1420d3f1041e2976c288bf9f98453d2bcb2b96b.title: Fixed-geometry length frontier
c1420d3f1041e2976c288bf9f98453d2bcb2b96b.body:
Let \(c>0\), let \(N_n\) be target sample sizes with \(N_n/n\to c\), let \(k_n\) be positive integers with \(k_n\to\infty\) and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\), let \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  Let \(\mathfrak g\) be a deterministic geometry array satisfying \cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class} at scale \(k_n\) and overlap parameter \(\varepsilon\).  Assume that, for every \(n\), every law in the fixed-geometry slice \(\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\) of \cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-slice} satisfies
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Two samples.)} \cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array} with target-to-source ratio \(c\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} \cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap} with overlap parameter \(\varepsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope.)} \cref{obj:ass:weight-envelope} at scale \(k_n\).
\item \textbf{(Second moment.)} \cref{obj:ass:weight-second-moment} at scale \(k_n\).
\item \textbf{(Degradation.)} \cref{obj:ass:degrading-array} at scale \(k_n\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
L_\alpha=\left(\frac{8}{\alpha\varepsilon^2}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
c_\alpha=\frac{3(1-\alpha)^2}{16},
\qquad
C_\alpha=\max\{2,4L_\alpha+8\varepsilon^{-2}\}.
\]
Then, for every fixed effective-strength threshold \(t_0>0\), the fixed-geometry minimax expected-length value \(V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)\) of \cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-value} satisfies
\[
c_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
\le
V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)
\le
C_\alpha\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
The constants \(c_\alpha\) and \(C_\alpha\) depend only on \(\alpha\) and \(\varepsilon\), uniformly over admissible deterministic geometry arrays \(\mathfrak g\).

a241b0f70bd36ef30d7ad7d6cece9900b59a8d47.title: Finite-cell sample-only attainment
a241b0f70bd36ef30d7ad7d6cece9900b59a8d47.body:
Let \(N_n\) and \(k_n\) be positive integer sequences, let \(c,\varepsilon,\alpha\in\mathbb R\), and suppose the following conditions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling ratio.)} \(c>0\) and \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap and coverage levels.)} \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Cell growth.)} \(k_n>0\) for every \(n\), \(k_n\to\infty\), and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Ambient carrier.)} For every \(n\), the measurable covariate space contains an injected copy of \(\{1,\ldots,k_n\}\) whose singleton images are measurable.
\item \textbf{(Finite-cell rows.)} For every row \(n\) and every transported array \(P\in\mathcal N_n\), with \(\mathcal N_n\) as in \cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class}, the row satisfies the two-sample condition in \cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}, the uniform finite-cell source condition in \cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}, and the degrading-array condition in \cref{obj:ass:degrading-array}.
\end{itemize}
Put
\[
B_c=32(1+c^{-1}),\qquad
L_{\alpha,c}=\left(\frac{2B_c}{\alpha}\right)^{1/2},\qquad
C_0=\max\{2,4\sqrt2\,L_{\alpha,c}+8B_c\}.
\]
Then \(C_0>0\), and there exists a sample-only finite-cell confidence-set sequence \(C=(C_n)\) in the feasible class \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{cell}}\) of \cref{obj:def:finite-cell-feasible-honesty} such that, for every \(n\) and every \(P\in\mathcal N_n\), \(C_n\) agrees \(P\)-almost surely under the two-sample law with the finite-cell score-inversion rule using critical constant \(L_{\alpha,c}\). Equivalently, on the finite-cell experiment, this rule is given by
\[
H_i=2(2Z_i-1),\qquad
\widehat p_{x,n}=\frac1{N_n}\sum_{j=1}^{N_n}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=x\},
\]
and, for \(G\in\{Y,D\}\),
\[
\widehat m_{G,n}(x)=\frac{k_n}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}H_iG_i,\qquad
\widehat M_{G,n}=\sum_{x=1}^{k_n}\widehat p_{x,n}\widehat m_{G,n}(x).
\]
For \(N_n\ge2\), define
\[
\widehat\kappa_{U,n}
=\frac{k_n}{N_n(N_n-1)}
\sum_{j\ne\ell}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=X_\ell^T\},\qquad
\widehat K_n=1+\widehat\kappa_{U,n},
\]
and set
\[
C_n=\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
|\widehat M_{Y,n}-\vartheta\widehat M_{D,n}|
\le L_{\alpha,c}\sqrt{\widehat K_n/n}\right\},
\]
with \(C_n=\Theta\) at indices for which \(N_n<2\). For every \(t_0>0\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n:\,t_n\ge t_0}
\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)]
\le
C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
Moreover, for every \(t_0>0\), the feasible finite-cell honest minimax risk satisfies
\[
\frac{3(1-\alpha)^2}{16}\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde C\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{cell}}}
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n:\,t_n\ge t_0}
\mathbb E_P[\lambda(\widetilde C_n)].
\]

c95549f54c2d17eb070d9a4d2c0de62d0d4a242e.title: Regular-cell score attainment
c95549f54c2d17eb070d9a4d2c0de62d0d4a242e.body:
Fix \(c,\varepsilon,\alpha,c_-,c_+\in\mathbb R\), target sample sizes \(N_n\), and cell counts \(k_n\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample-size ratio.)} \(0<c\) and \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap and coverage levels.)} \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
\item \textbf{(Regular cell constants.)} \(0<c_-\le 1\) and \(1\le c_+\).
\item \textbf{(Cell growth.)} \(k_n>0\) for every \(n\), \(k_n\to\infty\), and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\).
\item \textbf{(Measurable carrier.)} For every \(n\), the covariate carrier contains \(k_n\) injected measurable singleton cells.
\item \textbf{(Model restrictions.)} Every array \(P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) from \cref{obj:def:regular-finite-cell-class} with constants \(c,\varepsilon,c_-,c_+\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}, \cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap}, and \cref{obj:ass:degrading-array}.
\end{itemize}
On \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), let \(q_{x,n}=P_S^X(X=x)\) and define
\[
H_i=\frac{Z_i}{e(X_i)}-\frac{1-Z_i}{1-e(X_i)}.
\]
For \(G\in\{Y,D\}\), set
\[
\widehat p_{x,n}=\frac1{N_n}\sum_{j=1}^{N_n}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=x\},
\qquad
\widehat m_{G,n}(x)=\frac1{nq_{x,n}}\sum_{i=1}^n
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}H_iG_i,
\]
and
\[
\widehat M_{G,n}=\sum_{x=1}^{k_n}\widehat p_{x,n}\widehat m_{G,n}(x).
\]
For \(N_n\ge2\), set
\[
\widehat\kappa_{U,n}
=
\frac1{N_n(N_n-1)}\sum_{j\ne\ell}
\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_j^T=X_\ell^T\}}{q_{X_j^T,n}},
\qquad
\widehat K_n=1+\widehat\kappa_{U,n},
\]
and put \(C_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\Theta\) when \(N_n<2\).  Let
\[
B_{\varepsilon,c}=8(\varepsilon^{-2}+c^{-1}).
\]
For every \(L\ge\{2B_{\varepsilon,c}/\alpha\}^{1/2}\), define
\[
C_{0}=\max\{2,4\sqrt2L+8B_{\varepsilon,c}\}.
\]
Then \(0<C_0\), and there exists a regular-cell procedure \(C=(C_n)_{n\ge1}\) such that, for every \(n\) and every \(P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), \(C_n\) agrees almost surely under the two-sample law with
\[
C_n^{\mathrm{reg}}
=
\left\{\vartheta\in\Theta:
|\widehat M_{Y,n}-\vartheta\widehat M_{D,n}|
\le L\sqrt{\widehat K_n/n}\right\}
\]
for \(N_n\ge2\), together with the preceding convention for \(N_n<2\).  This procedure belongs to \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}\) from \cref{obj:def:regular-cell-feasible-honesty}.  Moreover, for every fixed \(t_0>0\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}:\,t_n\ge t_0}
\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)]
\le
C_0\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
For every fixed \(t_0>0\), the minimax risk over \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfies
\[
\frac{3(1-\alpha)^2}{16}\min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
\le
\inf_{C\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}}
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}:\,t_n\ge t_0}
\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)].
\]
Thus, with known regular source-cell probabilities and a known cell-varying propensity satisfying the stated overlap, the feasible regular-cell construction attains the oracle frontier order on \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\).

9e0187f5eb578c02adcb8ae5f3975e9e2f2394eb.title: Full-data support
9e0187f5eb578c02adcb8ae5f3975e9e2f2394eb.body:
The full-data law \(P_n^F\) satisfies
\[
P_n^F\{S\in\{0,1\},\ D(0),D(1)\in\{0,1\},\ Y(0),Y(1)\in[0,1]\}=1.
\]

4c0f1f73b21c98fc138c34aeed28fcc357b043c0.title: Two-sample array
4c0f1f73b21c98fc138c34aeed28fcc357b043c0.body:
The source observed sample \((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n\), target covariate sample \((X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}\), and target sample size \(N_n\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Source sampling.)} \((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n\sim P_S^{\otimes n}\).
\item \textbf{(Target sampling.)} \((X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}\sim P_T^{\otimes N_n}\).
\item \textbf{(Sample independence.)} \((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n\perp (X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n}\).
\item \textbf{(Sample-size ratio.)} \(N_n/n\to c\).
\end{itemize}

5dc94864827d6da889538ca574932c11b5f41a9d.title: Instrument overlap
5dc94864827d6da889538ca574932c11b5f41a9d.body:
For the source assignment propensity \(e(X)\) and instrument-overlap constant \(\varepsilon\),
\[
\varepsilon\le e(X)\le 1-\varepsilon
\]
\(P_S\)-almost surely.

452ea5a8f0b4d2d7f326132c7b17a98dfebec496.title: Source observation

9d834c88775dd452777da26156e03771a5e19e96.title: Instrument exclusion
9d834c88775dd452777da26156e03771a5e19e96.body:
For each \(z,s\in\{0,1\}\), under the full-data law \(P_n^F\),
\[
Y^Z(z)=Y(D(z))
\]
almost surely conditional on \(S=s\).

4f56f47db6818a8f6f21506c594c204d3ac1f44b.title: Instrument monotonicity
4f56f47db6818a8f6f21506c594c204d3ac1f44b.body:
For each \(s\in\{0,1\}\), under the full-data law \(P_n^F\),
\[
D(1)\ge D(0)
\]
almost surely conditional on \(S=s\).

2e9b5609fca898c4f0721e52df5fe921a4f20c7a.title: Outcome contrast transport
2e9b5609fca898c4f0721e52df5fe921a4f20c7a.body:
For \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\), where \(P_T\) is the target covariate law,
\[
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=0\right]
=
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=1\right].
\]

3fc94413cd144e038a7b8538fca813031145e7d0.title: Receipt contrast transport
3fc94413cd144e038a7b8538fca813031145e7d0.body:
Under the full-data law \(P_n^F\),
\[
\mathbb E_{X\mid S=0}\!\left[
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[D(1)-D(0)\mid X,S=0\right]
\right]
=
\mathbb E_{X\mid S=0}\!\left[
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[D(1)-D(0)\mid X,S=1\right]
\right].
\]

885374b4a4c071d2e8a66c91442ba0cf9cf3f513.title: Target complier positivity
885374b4a4c071d2e8a66c91442ba0cf9cf3f513.body:
Under the full-data law \(P_n^F\),
\[
P_n^F\!\left(D(1)>D(0)\mid S=0\right)>0.
\]

e0c53eef129bb48c1c62c40631cf49b251987d8a.title: Transport domination
e0c53eef129bb48c1c62c40631cf49b251987d8a.body:
On \(\mathcal X\), the target covariate law \(P_T\) is absolutely continuous with respect to the source covariate marginal \(P_S^X\):
\[
P_T\ll P_S^X.
\]

11af0780843bf84f44b9bb066661a9ae1f5fcdb1.title: Weight envelope
11af0780843bf84f44b9bb066661a9ae1f5fcdb1.body:
The target-to-source covariate density ratio satisfies
\[
0 \le w(X) \le 2k_n
\]
\(P_S\)-almost surely.

73961d2bc5f15e99cdc32cb6f10271c544f8b4a9.title: Weight second moment
73961d2bc5f15e99cdc32cb6f10271c544f8b4a9.body:
The second moment of the transport weight satisfies
\[
\kappa_n \le k_n .
\]

8502cd050175aaf4c789f0fd2e55ca876178f7fe.title: Degrading array rates

00db872bce09ce178f846cc9b84c44f7832f1ab7.title: Uniform finite-cell source
00db872bce09ce178f846cc9b84c44f7832f1ab7.body:
The source covariate marginal \(P_S^X\) is supported on exactly \(k_n\) measurable cells, assigns mass \(1/k_n\) to each cell, and satisfies
\[
e(X)=\frac12
\]
\(P_S\)-almost surely.

eda9d3f013229e30356af030598d473e5afbac00.title: Transported complier-effect model class \(\mathcal P_n\)
eda9d3f013229e30356af030598d473e5afbac00.body:
For each \(n\), the transported complier-effect model class is
\[
\mathcal P_n
=
\left\{
P=(P_n^F,e):
P \text{ satisfies the conditions below at index } n
\right\}.
\]
The conditions are:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Full-data and population structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:full-data-support,obj:ass:population-presence}\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument and observation structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:source-observation,obj:ass:iv-randomization,obj:ass:iv-exclusion,obj:ass:iv-monotonicity}\).
\item \textbf{(Transport and target-complier structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport,obj:ass:target-complier-positivity,obj:ass:transport-domination}\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope and degradation structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array}\).
\end{itemize}

6179012660896f748aaaecff5ed44dcbfd784a0e.title: Finite-cell submodel \(\mathcal N_n\)
6179012660896f748aaaecff5ed44dcbfd784a0e.body:
For each \(n\), the finite-cell submodel is
\[
\mathcal N_n
=
\left\{
P=(P_n^F,e):
P \text{ satisfies the conditions below at index } n
\right\}.
\]
The conditions are:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Full-data and population structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:full-data-support,obj:ass:population-presence}\).
\item \textbf{(Sampling structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument and observation structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:source-observation,obj:ass:iv-randomization,obj:ass:iv-exclusion,obj:ass:iv-monotonicity}\).
\item \textbf{(Transport and target-complier structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport,obj:ass:target-complier-positivity,obj:ass:transport-domination}\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope and degradation structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array}\).
\item \textbf{(Finite-cell source structure.)} \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}\).
\end{itemize}

d73707ed81dd5c49a5aa0c5d120520269d54d61b.title: Finite-cell oracle value $V_{\mathcal N}^\star(t_0)$

4856d209cc85d5873b8876e1f384aa9066898a8d.title: Score-inversion set $C_n$
4856d209cc85d5873b8876e1f384aa9066898a8d.body:
With oracle-known \(w\) and \(e\), define \(C_n\) by the following source-sample inversion procedure.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each \(\vartheta\in\Theta\), define the inverse-propensity score
\[
\psi_i(\vartheta)
=
w(X_i)\left\{\frac{Z_i}{e(X_i)}-\frac{1-Z_i}{1-e(X_i)}\right\}(Y_i-\vartheta D_i).
\]

\item Define the empirical score mean
\[
\widehat m_n(\vartheta)
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \psi_i(\vartheta).
\]

\item Define the oracle critical radius
\[
r_n
=
L_\alpha
\left\{
\frac{1}{n}\cdot \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n w(X_i)^2
\right\}^{1/2}.
\]

\item Output the score-inversion confidence set
\[
C_n
=
\left\{
\vartheta\in\Theta:
\left|\widehat m_n(\vartheta)\right|\le r_n
\right\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

2449180ef66112faf1ee3b2a52c9b4bdb8c3f010.title: Geometry handle \(\chi^2\) and \(\mathrm{TV}\)
2449180ef66112faf1ee3b2a52c9b4bdb8c3f010.body:
Fix an arbitrary admissible deterministic array \((P_S^X,w,e)\). Define
\[
\mu_n=\left(\frac{t_0\kappa_n}{n}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
p_n(x)=\frac{\mu_n w(x)}{\kappa_n}.
\]
For \(0<\alpha<1\), set
\[
\rho=\frac{1-\alpha}{8}.
\]
For every \(h\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
|h|\le \min\{1/4,\rho t_0^{-1/2}\},
\]
the law \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\) obtained by varying only the complier outcome mean satisfies, relative to its center \(Q_{n,0}^{\mathfrak g}\),
\[
1+\chi^2(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\Vert Q_{n,0}^{\mathfrak g})\le\exp(8t_0h^2),
\qquad
\|Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}-Q_{n,0}^{\mathfrak g}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le2\rho.
\]

2eabc5256cc10894cf87c7e84674af9fb8ff8d87.title: Least-favorable law \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\)
2eabc5256cc10894cf87c7e84674af9fb8ff8d87.body:
For \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\in\mathcal G\) and \(t_0>0\), \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\) is the joint observed-data law generated by the following construction. Set
\[
\mu_n=\left(\frac{t_0\kappa_n}{n}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
p_n(x)=\frac{\mu_nw(x)}{\kappa_n},
\qquad
\rho=\frac{1-\alpha}{8},
\qquad
H(t_0)=\min\{1/4,\rho t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
For \(|h|\le H(t_0)\), conditional on \(X=x\), assign compliance types by
\[
\Pr\{(D(0),D(1))=(0,1)\mid X=x\}=p_n(x),
\]
\[
\Pr\{(D(0),D(1))=(1,1)\mid X=x\}
=\Pr\{(D(0),D(1))=(0,0)\mid X=x\}
=\frac{1-p_n(x)}{2}.
\]
Set \(Y(0)=0\). For compliers,
\[
Y(1)\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2+h),
\]
and for always-takers and never-takers,
\[
Y(1)\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2).
\]
The same conditional full-data law is used in both populations, source encouragement is drawn with propensity \(e(X)\), and the resulting joint observed-data law together with the fixed oracle inputs is denoted by \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\).

02714aef87d5515e593b4e8d98735623d9bf177b.title: Admissible geometry class \(\mathcal G\)
02714aef87d5515e593b4e8d98735623d9bf177b.body:
\(\mathcal G\) is the class of deterministic arrays
\[
\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}
\]
such that, for each \(n\),
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Source marginal.)} \(P_S^X\) is a probability law on \(\mathcal X\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument overlap.)} The source assignment propensity satisfies
\[
e:\mathcal X\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon].
\]
\item \textbf{(Transport weights.)} The target-to-source covariate density ratio satisfies
\[
w:\mathcal X\to[0,2k_n],
\qquad
\mathbb E_S[w(X)]=1.
\]
\item \textbf{(Dispersion.)} The second moment of the transport weight is
\[
\kappa_n=\mathbb E_S[w(X)^2]\le k_n.
\]
\item \textbf{(Target law.)} For every measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\),
\[
P_T(A)=\mathbb E_S[w(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in A\}].
\]
\end{itemize}

739e3197acd5ac0f2ee6ce30e4f8a1fbee5757a4.title: Fixed-geometry slice \(\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\)
739e3197acd5ac0f2ee6ce30e4f8a1fbee5757a4.body:
For \(\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G\),
\[
\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)
=
\{P\in\mathcal P_n:(P_S^X,w,e)\text{ equals the index-}n\text{ component of }\mathfrak g\}.
\]

8243b536172474d61ab1639d1cc8827c0cfd9de3.title: Fixed-geometry oracle class \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathfrak g)\)
8243b536172474d61ab1639d1cc8827c0cfd9de3.body:
For \(\mathfrak g\in\mathcal G\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}\),
\[
\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathfrak g)
=
\left\{
(C_n)_{n\ge1}:
C_n=C_n\!\left((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n},w,e\right)\subseteq\Theta,\ 
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)}
P(\theta_T\in C_n)\ge1-\alpha
\right\}.
\]

200bd15671c916adae7e1e30da9e405937caff49.title: Fixed-geometry value \(V_{\mathfrak g}^\star(t_0)\)

daaf7a3627bc7da9794661a7049fd162dbb185da.title: Regular finite-cell class \(\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\)

48d0335688f90c40c550d72622f490b35e066095.title: Regular-cell feasible honesty class \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}\)
48d0335688f90c40c550d72622f490b35e066095.body:
\[
\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{reg}}
=
\left\{
(C_n)_{n\ge 1}:
C_n
=
C_n\left(
(O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,
(X_j^T)_{j=1}^{N_n},
(q_{x,n})_{x=1}^{k_n},\ne
\right)
\subseteq \Theta,\ 
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}}
P(\theta_T\in C_n)\ge 1-\alpha
\right\}.
\]

3a6022e734cbfb7aacdb19c66ad67be9c465ea0c.title: Oracle lower frontier
3a6022e734cbfb7aacdb19c66ad67be9c465ea0c.body:
Fix \(c>0\), an instrument-overlap constant \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and a noncoverage level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). There exist constants \(c_0>0\) and \(t_c>0\), depending only on \((\alpha,\varepsilon,c)\), such that the following holds for every measurable covariate space \(\mathcal X\).

Let \(N_n\) and \(k_n\) be integer sequences satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Target-source ratio.)} \(N_n/n\to c\).
\item \textbf{(Positive cells.)} \(k_n>0\) for every \(n\).
\item \textbf{(Diverging cells.)} \(k_n\to\infty\).
\item \textbf{(Sub-root growth.)} \(k_n/\sqrt n\to 0\).
\item \textbf{(Measurable carrier.)} For each \(n\), \(\mathcal X\) contains a measurable \(k_n\)-cell carrier.
\item \textbf{(Transported-IV model.)} Every array in the transported complier-effect class \(\mathcal P_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:full-data-support,obj:ass:population-presence,obj:ass:two-sample-array,obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:source-observation,obj:ass:iv-randomization,obj:ass:iv-exclusion,obj:ass:iv-monotonicity,obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport,obj:ass:target-complier-positivity,obj:ass:transport-domination,obj:ass:weight-envelope,obj:ass:weight-second-moment,obj:ass:degrading-array}\).
\item \textbf{(Finite-cell source.)} Every array in the finite-cell class \(\mathcal N_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class}\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:finite-cell-source}\).
\end{itemize}

Then, for every effective-strength threshold \(t_0>0\),
\[
  c_0 \min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
  \le V^\star(t_0)
\]
and
\[
  c_0 \min\{1,t_0^{-1/2}\}
  \le V_{\mathcal N}^\star(t_0),
\]
where \(V^\star(t_0)\) and \(V_{\mathcal N}^\star(t_0)\) are the oracle values in \(\cref{obj:def:oracle-value,obj:def:finite-cell-oracle-value}\). Moreover, whenever \(0<t_0\le t_c\),
\[
  c_0 \le V^\star(t_0).
\]

db713da9389da2ab15e7d3a7d251b2bb587dfcf6.title: Admissible geometry class \(\mathcal G\)
db713da9389da2ab15e7d3a7d251b2bb587dfcf6.body:
\(\mathcal G\) is the class of deterministic arrays
\[
\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}
\]
such that, for each \(n\),
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Source marginal.)} \(P_S^X\) is a probability law on \(\mathcal X\).
\item \textbf{(Instrument overlap.)} The source assignment propensity satisfies
\[
e:\mathcal X\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon].
\]
\item \textbf{(Transport weights.)} The target-to-source covariate density ratio satisfies
\[
w:\mathcal X\to[0,2k_n],
\qquad
\mathbb E_S[w(X)]=1.
\]
\item \textbf{(Weight dispersion.)} The second moment of the transport weight is
\[
\kappa_n=\mathbb E_S[w(X)^2]\le k_n.
\]
\item \textbf{(Target law.)} For every measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\),
\[
P_T(A)=\mathbb E_S[w(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in A\}].
\]
\end{itemize}

15aca69f2b34d2e0bfd10271264569f3082949ba.title: Least-favorable laws \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\)
15aca69f2b34d2e0bfd10271264569f3082949ba.body:
For \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\in\mathcal G\) and \(t_0>0\), \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\) is the joint observed-data law generated by the following construction. Set
\[
\mu_n=\left(\frac{t_0\kappa_n}{n}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
p_n(x)=\frac{\mu_nw(x)}{\kappa_n},
\qquad
\rho=\frac{1-\alpha}{8},
\qquad
H(t_0)=\min\{1/4,\rho t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
For a source observation \(O^S=(X,Z,D,Y)\), the inverse-propensity instrument score is
\[
H(O^S)=\frac{Z}{e(X)}-\frac{1-Z}{1-e(X)}.
\]
For \(|h|\le H(t_0)\), conditional on \(X=x\), assign compliance types by
\[
\Pr\{(D(0),D(1))=(0,1)\mid X=x\}=p_n(x),
\]
\[
\Pr\{(D(0),D(1))=(1,1)\mid X=x\}
=\Pr\{(D(0),D(1))=(0,0)\mid X=x\}
=\frac{1-p_n(x)}{2}.
\]
Set \(Y(0)=0\). For compliers,
\[
Y(1)\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2+h),
\]
and for always-takers and never-takers,
\[
Y(1)\sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(1/2).
\]
The same conditional full-data law is used in both populations, source encouragement is drawn with propensity \(e(X)\), and the resulting joint observed-data law together with the fixed oracle inputs is denoted by \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\).

27a415adda9e9993336ade5199d4a29bc9fc6041.title: Frontier risk \(R((C_n),t_0)\)
27a415adda9e9993336ade5199d4a29bc9fc6041.body:
For a confidence set \(C_n\), let \(\lambda(C_n)\) denote the Lebesgue length of \(C_n\cap\Theta\). The effective identification strength is
\[
t_n=\frac{n\mu_n^2}{\kappa_n}.
\]
For \(t_0>0\), the limiting worst-case expected length above effective strength \(t_0\) is
\[
R((C_n),t_0)
=
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n:\,t_n\ge t_0}
\mathbb E_P[\lambda(C_n)].
\]

33f6721465db425ebd9230bb9d05ba4a93e278ae.title: Least-favorable law \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\)
33f6721465db425ebd9230bb9d05ba4a93e278ae.body:
For \(\mathfrak g=(P_S^X,w,e)_{n\ge1}\in\mathcal G\), \(t_0>0\), and \(|h|\le H(t_0)\), \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\) is the joint observed-data law generated by the following construction. Set
\[
\mu_n=\left(\frac{t_0\kappa_n}{n}\right)^{1/2},
\qquad
p_n(x)=\frac{\mu_nw(x)}{\kappa_n},
\qquad
\rho=\frac{1-\alpha}{8},
\qquad
H(t_0)=\min\{1/4,\rho t_0^{-1/2}\}.
\]
For a source observation \(O^S=(X,Z,D,Y)\), the inverse-propensity instrument score is
\[
H_i=\frac{Z}{e(X)}-\frac{1-Z}{1-e(X)}.
\]
Conditional on \(X=x\), assign compliance types by
\[
\mathbb P\{(D(0),D(1))=(0,1)\mid X=x\}=p_n(x),
\]
\[
\mathbb P\{(D(0),D(1))=(1,1)\mid X=x\}
=
\mathbb P\{(D(0),D(1))=(0,0)\mid X=x\}
=
\frac{1-p_n(x)}{2}.
\]
Set \(Y(0)=0\). For compliers,
\[
Y(1)\sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2+h),
\]
and for always-takers and never-takers,
\[
Y(1)\sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2).
\]
The same conditional full-data law is used in both populations, source encouragement is drawn with propensity \(e(X)\), and the resulting joint observed-data law together with the fixed oracle inputs is denoted by \(Q_{n,h}^{\mathfrak g}\).

08302d874d8f461b1038dd262602091f2229ae16.title: Second-moment envelope
08302d874d8f461b1038dd262602091f2229ae16.body:

=

052202107ae99abacbb847ee67db320ffeacd57f.body:

=

e297b251e6a62dd0d71e7285975a8c718356252c.body:

ff692051039f32d93166e3d236da737f8e91b63f.title: Frontier risk $R((C_n),t_0)$
ff692051039f32d93166e3d236da737f8e91b63f.body:

2bbafc52f6bb95aa9219b6b3468667fcb81e5c40.title: Outcome transport
2bbafc52f6bb95aa9219b6b3468667fcb81e5c40.body:
The source conditional outcome contrast is
\[
\Delta_Y(x)
=
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=1\right].
\]
For \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\), where \(P_T\) is the target covariate law,
\[
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[Y^Z(1)-Y^Z(0)\mid X=x,S=0\right]
=
\Delta_Y(x).
\]

eabf2208216cc03a74300699661f5cdf22fef30d.title: Receipt transport
eabf2208216cc03a74300699661f5cdf22fef30d.body:

\[

=
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[D(1)-D(0)\mid X=x,S=1\right].

Under the full-data law \(P_n^F\),
\[
\mathbb E_{X\mid S=0}\!\left[
\mathbb E_{P_n^F}\!\left[D(1)-D(0)\mid X,S=0\right]
\right]
=
\mathbb E_{X\mid S=0}\!\left[\Delta_D(X)\right].
\]

e6d2f3824e195373d87ff9cd0e661c9e082ba651.title: Finite-cell class inhabitation
e6d2f3824e195373d87ff9cd0e661c9e082ba651.body:
Suppose the following conditions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Measurable finite cells.)} For every \(n\), there is an injection from \(\{1,\ldots,k_n\}\) into the covariate space \(\mathcal X\) such that each injected singleton is measurable.
\item \textbf{(Sample-size ratio.)} The constant \(c\) satisfies \(0<c\), and \(N_n/n\to c\) as in \cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}.
\item \textbf{(Instrument overlap.)} The constant \(\varepsilon\) satisfies \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), as in \cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap}.
\item \textbf{(Cell-count sequence.)} For every \(n\), \(k_n>0\), with \(k_n\to\infty\) and
\[
\frac{k_n}{\sqrt n}\to 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(n\), there exists a transported array law \(P\), consisting of full-data and observed source laws together with the associated propensity, assignment-outcome, assignment-contrast, and receipt-contrast functions, such that \(P\) belongs to the finite-cell submodel \(\mathcal N_n\) of \cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class}.

9ad35e455e99724a129e0ff113f8fbee7586e7e8.title: Source observation facts
9ad35e455e99724a129e0ff113f8fbee7586e7e8.body:
Let \(P\) belong to the transported complier-effect model class \(\mathcal P_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), for the sample-size array \(N_n\), envelope scale \(k_n\), target-to-source ratio \(c\), and instrument-overlap constant \(\varepsilon\). Let \(P_{\mathrm{assign},S}\) denote the assigned-source overlay on \((F,Z)\), where \(F=(S,X,D(0),D(1),Y(0),Y(1))\), and let \(P_S\) be its observed-source image under \((F,Z)\mapsto (X,Z,D(Z),Y(D(Z)))\). Write \(P_S^X\) for the source covariate marginal and
\[
H(O^S)
=
\frac{\mathbf 1\{Z=1\}}{e(X)}
-
\frac{\mathbf 1\{Z=0\}}{1-e(X)} .
\]
Then \(P_{\mathrm{assign},S}\) and \(P_S\) are probability measures, the full-data marginal of \(P_{\mathrm{assign},S}\) is \(P_n^F(\cdot\mid S=1)\), and the observed outcome satisfies \(Y\in[0,1]\) \(P_S\)-almost surely. Moreover, for every measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\),
\[
P_S\{X\in A,\ Z=1\}
=
\int_A e(x)\,dP_S^X(x),
\]
\[
\int_{\{X\in A\}} H(O^S)Y\,dP_S
=
\int_A \Delta_Y(x)\,dP_S^X(x),
\]
and
\[
\int_{\{X\in A\}} H(O^S)D\,dP_S
=
\int_A \Delta_D(x)\,dP_S^X(x).
\]
Finally, \(\Delta_Y(X)\in[-1,1]\) and \(\Delta_D(X)\in[0,1]\) hold \(P_S^X\)-almost surely.

9c57256ffffc338f8f16850672cae6c3a85eb14c.title: Regular class is inhabited
9c57256ffffc338f8f16850672cae6c3a85eb14c.body:
Assume the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Finite measurable cells.)} For every \(n\), the covariate space \(\mathcal X\) contains \(k_n\) distinct points, indexed by \(\{1,\ldots,k_n\}\), whose singletons are measurable.
\item \textbf{(Sample-size ratio.)} The asymptotic target-to-source sample-size ratio \(c\) satisfies \(0<c\), and \(N_n/n\to c\) as in \cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}.
\item \textbf{(Instrument overlap.)} The instrument-overlap constant \(\varepsilon\) satisfies \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), as in \cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap}.
\item \textbf{(Regular-cell bounds.)} The fixed constants \(c_-\) and \(c_+\) satisfy \(0<c_-\le 1\le c_+\).
\item \textbf{(Cell-count growth.)} For every \(n\), \(k_n>0\), and \(k_n\to\infty\) with \(k_n/\sqrt n\to 0\), as in \cref{obj:ass:degrading-array,obj:ass:weight-envelope}.
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(n\), there exists a transported array \(P\), consisting of full-data laws, assigned-source laws, propensities, assignment-outcome maps, assignment contrasts, and receipt contrasts with the usual measurability structure, such that \(P\in\mathcal N_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), the regular finite-cell model class of \cref{obj:def:regular-finite-cell-class}. Equivalently, the finite-cell witness in \(\mathcal N_n\) of \cref{obj:def:finite-cell-class} can be chosen so that its source cell probabilities satisfy
\[
q_{x,n}=1/k_n
\]
on the \(k_n\) measurable cells, and hence
\[
c_-/k_n\le q_{x,n}\le c_+/k_n .
\]

ea3ebc106a68c6ac0f9fea79276c692256320e3b.title: Fixed slice inhabitation
ea3ebc106a68c6ac0f9fea79276c692256320e3b.body:
Let \(\mathfrak g\), the deterministic geometry array, be fixed, and let \(N_n\) and \(k_n\) be integer-valued sequences. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Admissible geometry.)} The geometry \(\mathfrak g\) is admissible for the envelope sequence \(k_n\) and the instrument-overlap constant \(\varepsilon\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:admissible-geometry-class}\).
\item \textbf{(Sample-size ratio.)} The constant \(c\), the asymptotic target-to-source sample-size ratio, satisfies \(c>0\), and \(N_n/n\to c\) as in \(\cref{obj:ass:two-sample-array}\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap level.)} The instrument-overlap constant satisfies \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), as in \(\cref{obj:ass:instrument-overlap}\).
\item \textbf{(Strength threshold.)} The fixed effective-strength threshold satisfies \(t_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope growth.)} The envelope sequence satisfies \(k_n>0\) for every \(n\), \(k_n\to\infty\), and \(k_n/\sqrt n\to0\), as in \(\cref{obj:ass:degrading-array,obj:ass:weight-envelope}\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\), there exists a transported-array law \(P\) such that \(P\in\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g)\), the fixed-geometry slice of \(\cref{obj:def:fixed-geometry-slice}\), and its effective identification strength \(t_n(P)=n\mu_n(P)^2/\kappa_n(P)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:frontier-risk}\) satisfies
\[
t_n(P)\ge t_0 .
\]
Equivalently, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the strength-restricted fixed-geometry slice
\[
\{P\in\mathcal P_n(\mathfrak g): t_n(P)\ge t_0\}
\]
is nonempty.

603419f96d0852469f435740f1f35d52d7e3fd2c.title: Contrast integrability
603419f96d0852469f435740f1f35d52d7e3fd2c.body:
Fix an index \(n\), a transported array \(P\), sample-size and envelope schedules \(N_n\) and \(k_n\), a target-to-source ratio \(c\), and an instrument-overlap parameter \(\varepsilon\). Suppose that \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Then the source conditional outcome contrast \(\Delta_Y\) and the source conditional receipt contrast \(\Delta_D\) are integrable with respect to the source covariate marginal \(P_S^X\):
\[
\Delta_Y\in L^1(P_S^X)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Delta_D\in L^1(P_S^X).
\]

8cb2bd474b25527d225e3f3c3614bbb3bf8b892b.body:

\]

4f88740aa9a810ec6b803608d0b498369739b0a3.title: Source observation facts
4f88740aa9a810ec6b803608d0b498369739b0a3.body:
Let \(P\) belong to the transported complier-effect model class \(\mathcal P_n\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), for the sample-size array \(N_n\), envelope scale \(k_n\), target-to-source ratio \(c\), and instrument-overlap constant \(\varepsilon\). In particular, the source-observation quantities below are governed by \(\cref{obj:ass:full-data-support,obj:ass:two-sample-array,obj:ass:instrument-overlap,obj:ass:source-observation,obj:ass:iv-exclusion,obj:ass:iv-monotonicity,obj:ass:outcome-transport,obj:ass:receipt-transport,obj:ass:transport-domination}\). Let \(P_{\mathrm{assign},S}\) denote the assigned-source overlay on \((F,Z)\), where \(F=(S,X,D(0),D(1),Y(0),Y(1))\), and let \(P_S\) be its observed-source image under \((F,Z)\mapsto (X,Z,D(Z),Y(D(Z)))\). Write \(P_S^X\) for the source covariate marginal and
\[
H(O^S)
=
\frac{\mathbf 1\{Z=1\}}{e(X)}
-
\frac{\mathbf 1\{Z=0\}}{1-e(X)} .
\]
Then \(P_{\mathrm{assign},S}\) and \(P_S\) are probability measures, the full-data marginal of \(P_{\mathrm{assign},S}\) is \(P_n^F(\cdot\mid S=1)\), and the observed outcome satisfies \(Y\in[0,1]\) \(P_S\)-almost surely. Moreover, for every measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\),
\[
P_S\{X\in A,\ Z=1\}
=
\int_A e(x)\,dP_S^X(x),
\]
\[
\int_{\{X\in A\}} H(O^S)Y\,dP_S
=
\int_A \Delta_Y(x)\,dP_S^X(x),
\]
and
\[
\int_{\{X\in A\}} H(O^S)D\,dP_S
=
\int_A \Delta_D(x)\,dP_S^X(x).
\]
Finally, \(\Delta_Y(X)\in[-1,1]\) and \(\Delta_D(X)\in[0,1]\) hold \(P_S^X\)-almost surely.
